What this question exposed (all generalizable, all saved):

1. New document section — "Profile of the Economy" front-matter charts. Mid-2000s Bulletins open with a narrative "Profile of the Economy" section before the numbered Table exhibits, carrying small charts (Payroll Employment, GDP, unemployment, CPI). These are value-reading questions, distinct from the existing "count visual features" category. Saved the locating method (search text for "Profile of the Economy" / chart title) and reading approach.

2. Nested-averaging pitfall — "mean of the average monthly change from end-Q1 to end-Q2 across years" is a two-level average: per-year = span change ÷ MONTH count (Mar→Jun = 3 months, divide by 3), then mean across the inclusive YEAR count (3). The divisor traps (month count, not quarter count, not year count) are the generalizable part. Also noted payroll charts often plot the monthly change directly, so you average the 3 bars.

Both went into references/profile-of-economy-charts.md with the worked 202.333 example, plus a short pointer in SKILL.md.
